Method of Attack: Backdoor in the xz/liblzma library that enables remote, unprivileged systems to connect to public SSH ports and execute malicious code
Malicious script in build-to-host.m4 checks for specific conditions (e.g., AMD64 architecture, glibc) and unpacks obfuscated/encrypted bash stages and a binary backdoor from test files
IFUNC function in glibc is used maliciously to perform runtime hooking/redirection of OpenSSH's authentication routines
Impacted Systems: Red Hat’s Fedora 40 and Fedora Rawhide Linux distributions
Attack Vector: Supply chain attack via compromised upstream xz/liblzma library
Indicators of Compromise: Slower SSH logins and high CPU usage
Valgrind errors on Debian sid installations
Malicious code in test files (tests/files/bad-3-corrupt_lzma2.xz, tests/files/good-large_compressed.lzma)
Loss of application hardening functions in the malicious version of liblzma
